4. Discovery limits and manual-field guidance

The engine records subject and issuer common names, validity dates, signature algorithm, public-key algorithm, key size or curve, and the self-signed and CA flags. It does not record
serial numbers, fingerprints, subject alternative names, key usage or extended key usage, organisation fields, or OCSP and CRL locations.

A certificate is identified across scans by a hash of its recorded attributes. Two different certificates that agree on every recorded attribute would be shown as one; this is not expected in
practice because validity dates have one-second precision.

Expiry is computed from the notAfter date as of the generation date of this document and can differ from the flag raised when the scan ran.

Whether a certificate is managed, orphaned or in production use needs an authoritative PKI or CMDB inventory, so owner and business-system columns are left for the assessor.

Owner and Business system are intentionally blank. Record the accountable owner and the business system each certificate protects from your PKI or CMDB inventory; do not infer
ownership from the file path or the name of the source.
Chain flags are factual: a certificate is 'Signed by' a file only when that issuer certificate is in the estate, and 'Issuer not in estate' means no certificate with the issuer's name was found.

5. Validation approach
Detection is deterministic: rule tables, parsers and pattern matching. Every CycloneDX 1.6 bill of materials the engine emits is validated

Each compliance requirement receives one of four outcomes: pass, fail, not evidenceable from a bill of materials, or out of scope. Coverage
% = pass / (pass + fail), where pass includes requirements passed on attached evidence. Not-evidenceable and out-of-scope requirements
are reported as separate counts and are never counted as passes. Attaching attestation evidence to a scan can move a not-evidenceable
requirement to pass with evidence.
Coverage = (Pass + Pass with evidence) / (Pass + Pass with evidence + Fail). Not evidenceable and out-of-scope requirements are shown
as their own counts and are never counted as passes.
